ety.text: Borrowed from French bathysphère, from Ancient Greek βάθος (báthos, “depth”) and σφαῖρα (sphaîra, “sphere”).
From ба́тя (bátja) + -ко (-ko); originally a diminutive. Cognates include Ukrainian ба́тько (bátʹko), Belarusian ба́цька (bácʹka). This spelling is probably influenced by Ukrainian.

s.g: large language model (a type of neural network specializing in language, typically including billions of parameters)

s.g: to splash out, to spill out
to express (oneself), to say, to tell, to pronounce

ety.text: Inherited from Old East Slavic зѫбъ (zǫbŭ), from Proto-Slavic *zǫbъ, from Proto-Balto-Slavic *źámbas, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵómbʰos. Cognate to Old Church Slavonic зѫбъ (zǫbŭ).
From Medieval Greek κάτεργον (kátergon, “galley; penal labor”), from Ancient Greek κάτεργος (kátergos).
